subject: Renewal: territory onramp & data jurisdiction addendum
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@aureliahealth.com>, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: territory onramp & data jurisdiction addendum

Hi Oliver / Aurelia procurement team —

Hope you had a good weekend. As we approach your renewal (term ends 2026-09-30) I wanted to align on three items that will affect the new term and SOW: EU node residency, a staged APAC pilot, and cross-region failover for business continuity. High level proposal below; attached is a draft addendum ("draft-territory-addendum_v2.pdf").

Key asks from Aurelia so we can finalize pricing and paperwork:
- Confirm whether EU residency must be primary (all EU traffic stays in EU) or if an EU-primary with APAC warm-standby is acceptable.
- Confirm appetite for a short Dedicated capacity uplift (+20% committed GPUs) for the first 90 days of migration to guarantee throughput during cutover.
- Procurement timeline for PO / signature; legal will need the DPA.

Proposed terms (high level):
- 12-month renewal with option to extend to 24 months at a 7% price break.
- Addendum to pin EU residency for production traffic to Frankfurt region; APAC (Singapore) to be staged as warm standby for DR and for staged rollout — traffic will fail over only under defined SLO breach scenarios.
- Dedicated capacity uplift priced as a one-time commitment credit rather than an ongoing rate.

Next steps: if this high level looks OK I can circulate a 1-page amendment + DPA for legal. Would you be available for a 30-min call next week to lock timeline?

Attachments: draft-territory-addendum_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@aureliahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com, Emma Liu <emma.liu@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal: territory onramp & data jurisdiction addendum

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we set the meeting:

1) Data residency: Our legal team needs EU-residency for all PHI-related traffic. Can Redwood confirm the mechanism for ensuring routing stays in-region (i.e., regional routing + enforceable contract language)?

2) APAC pilot: We like the idea of a staged rollout but need a clear failback plan and a schedule for a DR runbook test. Can you provide the SLA hit/credit mechanism if failover triggers?

3) Pricing: Can you send a delta for the dedicated uplift as an explicit line item (one-time spend + monthly delta if kept beyond 90 days)?

Procurement timeline: We aim to have a signed PO by end of July if legal signs off on the DPA and amendment.

Also — please share the DPA; our GC needs to review it.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Schmidt
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Aurelia Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: territory onramp & data jurisdiction addendum (pricing options)

Team —

Drafted three clean options we can offer Aurelia; I'm copying the numbers so we can agree what to put in the amendment:

Option A (Safe): EU-primary (Frankfurt) + APAC warm-standby; 12-mo renewal; Dedicated uplift = one-time $45k for 90 days; monthly after 90d (if kept) = $6k/month; SLA credit 5% of monthly spend if failover is unplanned.

Option B (Balanced): EU-primary + limited APAC seeding for non-PHI traffic; 12-mo renewal with 10% committed increase in request units (measured by RTX); one-time uplift $30k; monthly after = $4k/month; SLA credit 3%.

Option C (Aggressive go-live): Full geo-seeding (all traffic in both regions) — requires stronger DPA terms and HSM KMS for key separation; 24-mo commit with 12% discount; Dedicated uplift $75k.

Recommendation: Start with Option A but offer to move to B within 60 days for traffic partitioning and lower run-rate if Aurelia is willing to accept non-PHI seeding in APAC initially. This gives us a path to reduce cost risk.

Also recommend we include a 30-day blackout on major changes during final cutover and a 2-week joint DR run to prove failover.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@aureliahealth.com>, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 14:07:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal: territory onramp & data jurisdiction addendum

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the quick questions. Attached is an updated one-page amendment that implements Option A language (EU-primary + APAC warm-standby) plus a DPA for legal (DPA_Aurelia_signed.pdf). Key points called out in the amendment:

- Binding routing policy: "Production traffic originating from EU-designated customer tenants will be routed to EU nodes. Redwood will use geo-routing + tenant-binding to prevent egress to APAC for PHI-tagged requests except during an explicit failover event as defined in the SLA."
- Dedicated uplift: one-time 90-day commitment credit $45,000.
- Failover SLA: automatic failover allowed only after an SLO breach window of 60s latency or availability < 99.5% for 15 consecutive minutes; SLA credit defined as 5% of monthly invoice for any unplanned failover.
- DR testing: joint runbook with two maintenance windows; Redwood will provide a checklist (sla-failover-checklist.xlsx) and support engineers for the first run.

Can you confirm procurement's PO timing? If Aurelia can sign the amendment by 2026-07-15 we can schedule the APAC pilot for the week of 2026-08-10 and do the DR run on 2026-08-17.

Attachments: draft-territory-addendum_v2.pdf, DPA_Aurelia_signed.pdf, sla-failover-checklist.xlsx

Thanks for moving quickly on this — happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through the amendment line-by-line.

Best,
Karthik
From: Oliver Schmidt <oliver.schmidt@aureliahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com, Emma Liu <emma.liu@aureliahealth.com>
Bcc: legal-team@aureliahealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 16:32:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal: territory onramp & data jurisdiction addendum

Karthik —

Thanks for the updated amendment and for laying out the runbook items. We ran the DPA by GC and the changes look acceptable — we've attached the countersigned DPA for your records (DPA_Aurelia_signed.pdf). Procurement will issue a PO for Option A by 2026-09-01; we will mark the PO to include the one-time dedicated uplift line item.

We agree to the DR run week of 2026-08-17 — engineering will coordinate times with your team (Emma Liu will be the lead). Please consider this confirmation that Aurelia accepts the amendment language pending PO.

On another note: we'll want a short executive summary for our board that calls out the residency assurance and standby plan — can someone from Redwood produce a 1-pager?

Thanks,
Oliver

--
